author: ojiudezue
title: Pre-Deploy Zero-Bugs Gate is mandatory before every deploy.sh
summary: v4.7.4.3 was tagged and pushed to GitHub with literal `<<<<<<< HEAD` / `=======` / `>>>>>>>` markers in `__init__.py`, `config_flow.py`, and `QUALITY_CONTEXT.md`. The merge command produced conflicts; the deploy script ran anyway. Any HACS install would have hit `SyntaxError: invalid syntax`. Caused by my own process failure: I ignored CONFLICT messages from the git merge output and ran deploy.sh without validating. User: 'We need to make sure we ship zero bugs.' Recovery: replaced with v4.7.4.4 within one hour. Permanent process change: a 4-gate validation MUST run before every deploy.sh invocation.

decisions.decision: Mandatory 4-gate pre-deploy validation: conflict markers + py_compile + cycle tests + suite baseline diff
decisions.why: The existing test suite uses source-grep / AST inspection and passed cleanly even with broken syntax in the same file — because the patterns it greps for were structurally present around the conflict markers. The first runtime touchpoint was HACS install on a live HA. By that time the GitHub release was already public and another user (in a future multi-install world) could have downloaded it. The gate must catch syntax-breaking errors BEFORE deploy.sh ever runs.
decisions.blast_radius: Captured as `feedback_pre_deploy_zero_bugs_gate.md` in auto-memory. Codified in CLAUDE.md release process section. All future cycle close-outs run the gate.

decisions.decision: Source-grep AST tests are necessary but not sufficient for the test suite
decisions.why: AST patterns can be satisfied by code that doesn't compile — Python's grammar allows nested expressions inside string-context contexts where the grep pattern matches. py_compile is the cheap insurance that catches what the grep tests can't. Bundled into v4.7.5 task #112 (config_flow runtime smoke tests) so we get a second layer of import-time validation too.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Add py_compile to the existing test suite as a fixture, run on every test invocation
alternatives_considered.why_rejected: Considered but not enough. py_compile inside pytest passes if the file compiles. The bug here was that the AGENT pipeline ran tests BEFORE the merge — so the green test result was stale by the time deploy.sh ran. The gate has to run between merge and deploy, not before merge.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Block deploy.sh script-level on conflict markers (modify the script)
alternatives_considered.why_rejected: Useful AND should happen — but the human/agent operator should also be running the gate manually as the first line of defense. Script gates can be bypassed; behavioral memory cannot.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Move to CI-gated releases (GitHub Actions runs the gate before tag is pushed)
alternatives_considered.why_rejected: Right answer long-term. Not in scope for this immediate response — the agent-level process rule closes the gap today without infra work.

implications: Builder agents will now refuse to declare a cycle done if conflict markers exist anywhere in changed files.
Deployer skill (`/deploy`) should incorporate the gate before invoking deploy.sh. TODO: update the skill definition.
The post-mortem doc for this incident becomes a reference for the discipline: 'this is what happens when you skip the gate.' Captured in v4.7.x stretch retrospective.
User trust impact: ANY future broken release will be a process-level concern, not just a code-level one.
follow_up: Update `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` to bake the 4-gate validation into Step 0 (before tests).
Consider adding `git merge --no-commit` followed by explicit conflict check to scripts/deploy.sh.
Add a CI workflow `gate.yml` that runs the 4 gates on every PR to develop and master.
ship_target: Process change effective immediately 2026-05-29; tooling follow-ups (skill + script) TBD
